policy: Every number in a row's inputs was read from the source listed on that row; nothing is estimated to fill a gap.

official_start_utc is filled only when the official page states the time zone (UTC, GMT, or a named zone such as Europe/Dublin in the page's calendar export). A local clock printed without a zone is shown as printed and left out of the UTC column, following the project's FL-148 rule; such rows cannot be graded HIGH.
Press sources (BBC, RTE, HoganStand, Tuam Herald) are listed as press, never as official, and are used only for team news.
Rows without an entry here are published as market-anchored LOW lines: OLBG's printed price, de-margined, with no form input.

BCCI - 1st T20I scorecard: India 230/6 beat New Zealand 225/4
BCCI - 2nd T20I: India 181/6 beat New Zealand 180/5
New Zealand Cricket scoring centre - 3rd T20I

form.basis: results in this T20I series (BCCI scorecards); edge -0.04 because New Zealand are at home

188852.form_text: India lead the series 2-0: 230/6 chasing 225/4 in the 1st T20I, 181/6 chasing 180/5 in the 2nd.
188852.prose: India go to Wellington 2-0 up and have now chased targets of 226 and 181 in this series, which tells you their batting depth holds up under scoreboard pressure. Sanju Samson's 67 set up the first chase and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 finished the second, so the runs are not resting on one player. New Zealand have been close both times and Mitchell Santner's 4-21 shows they can squeeze the middle overs, but a home side that has lost two tight finishes needs more than spin to turn this around. India to complete the sweep.
